Ascr.hero_subtitle: The ASCR provides the policy framework endorsed by the African Union. Green Gate provides the operational software that turns that framework into collected revenue. Together, they enable sovereign carbon tax collection across the continent.

Ascr.int_compliance_desc: ASCR's third-party verification framework applies to Green Gate's audit trail — hash-chained records provide the transparency required for ASCR certification.
Ascr.int_interop_desc: Green Gate's API is designed for integration with ASCR's digital registry infrastructure, enabling automatic data exchange between the collection system and the continental registry.
Ascr.cta_desc: If your country is part of the ASCR framework or considering sovereign carbon tax collection, Green Gate provides the operational infrastructure to make it real.

DashboardPages.simulator_faq_q1: How is the carbon tax calculated?
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a1: The tax is based on estimated CO2 emissions using the IMO SFOC (Specific Fuel Oil Consumption) methodology. Emissions = fuel consumption x CO2 emission factor. Tax = emissions x official rate x zone multiplier.
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_q2: What is the difference between EEZ tax and port tax?
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a2: The EEZ tax covers transit in the Exclusive Economic Zone (200 NM). The port tax applies during port stay (auxiliary engines). Rates and multipliers may differ by zone.
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a3: No. This estimate is indicative. The final invoice (pro-forma) is calculated from actual AIS data recorded during your passage in the EEZ and at port.
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a4: Specific Fuel Oil Consumption (g/kWh) measures fuel consumption per unit of energy produced by the engine. Each vessel type has an average SFOC. For a precise estimate, use your vessel's actual SFOC.
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_q5: How can I reduce my carbon tax?
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a5: Reduce speed (slow steaming), use low CO2 factor fuels (LNG, methanol), optimize port stay duration, or obtain carbon credits via certified Green Gate projects.
DashboardPages.simulator_faq_a6: Yes. Scientific research vessels, military ships, and certain vessels under bilateral agreements may benefit from partial or full exemptions. Contact the port authority for more information.

TermsOfService.section_04_li1: Provide accurate, complete, and current information during registration and at all times during use of the Platform.
TermsOfService.section_04_li2: Maintain the confidentiality of their credentials and immediately notify the SMCA at security@smca.gov.sl if they suspect unauthorized access to their account.
TermsOfService.section_04_li3: Use the Platform exclusively for its intended lawful purposes — tax compliance, invoice management, fleet monitoring, and reporting — and not for any commercial, competitive intelligence, or unauthorized purpose.
TermsOfService.section_04_li4: Comply with all applicable laws, including the Maritime Carbon Act 2024, Somaliland Tax Administration Act 2023, IMO MARPOL Annex VI, and international maritime conventions to which Somaliland is a party.
TermsOfService.section_04_li5: Accept that all actions performed on the Platform are recorded in an immutable audit log that may be used as evidence in administrative or criminal proceedings.
TermsOfService.section_04_li6: Not circumvent, disable, or interfere with any security feature of the Platform, including authentication mechanisms, rate limiters, and access controls.
TermsOfService.section_04_li7: Ensure that all vessels under your management are correctly declared in the Platform, including accurate IMO numbers, flag states, and gross tonnage.
TermsOfService.section_04_li8: Respond to pro-forma invoices and payment requests within the timeframes specified in the Maritime Carbon Act 2024 (48 hours for standard invoices, 24 hours for urgent enforcement notices).
TermsOfService.section_04_li9: Notify the SMCA of any change in fleet composition, ownership transfer, or flag change within 5 business days.
TermsOfService.section_05_highlight: The maritime carbon tax is a sovereign fiscal instrument of the Republic of Somaliland, established under the Maritime Carbon Act 2024 and applicable to all commercial vessels of 400 GT or above entering, transiting, or remaining in the Somaliland EEZ. Payment of carbon tax is a legal obligation, not optional, and non-payment constitutes a fiscal offense.
TermsOfService.section_05_row1_trigger: Vessel crossing the EEZ boundary inbound
TermsOfService.section_05_row2_trigger: Vessel berthing at Berbera, Zeila, or other recognized ports
TermsOfService.section_05_row3_trigger: Vessel transiting without port call (≥12h in EEZ)
TermsOfService.section_05_row4_trigger: Each additional 24h period of port stay beyond 48h
TermsOfService.section_05_p1: Carbon tax rates are calculated per tonne of CO₂-equivalent emissions, estimated using the IMO Energy Efficiency Operational Indicator (EEOI) methodology or, where engine data is available, direct SFOC-based calculation. Rates are published in the Tax Configuration by vessel category and jurisdiction zone, as visible in the Platform Tax Settings.
TermsOfService.section_05_p2: Vessels may apply for exemptions under Art. 17 of the Maritime Carbon Act 2024 (military vessels under bilateral agreements, humanitarian aid vessels, distress vessels). Exemptions require ministerial approval and are time-limited. Fraudulent exemption applications are a criminal offense.
TermsOfService.section_06_li1: Pro-forma invoices are generated automatically by the Platform based on AIS data and tax configuration. They are legally valid demand documents under Somaliland tax law.
TermsOfService.section_06_li2: Payment may be made via: (i) SWIFT bank transfer to the SMCA Treasury account, (ii) approved maritime escrow services, or (iii) carbon credit retirement (where eligible).
TermsOfService.section_06_li3: Invoices unpaid within the stipulated window are escalated to OVERDUE status. Overdue vessels are subject to port gate lock, vessel detention orders, and escalation to the Ministry of Justice.
TermsOfService.section_06_li4: Payment disputes must be filed in writing within 10 business days of invoice issuance to disputes@smca.gov.sl. Filing a dispute does not suspend the payment obligation unless the SMCA issues an explicit stay of enforcement.
TermsOfService.section_06_li5: Overpayments are refunded within 30 business days, or credited against future tax liabilities at the operator's option.
TermsOfService.section_06_warning: Port Gate Lock: Vessels with OVERDUE status may be subject to a Port Gate Lock Order, preventing departure from Berbera or Zeila port until full payment is confirmed. The SMCA is not liable for any commercial losses arising from lawful detention of non-compliant vessels.
TermsOfService.section_07_p1: The following actions are strictly prohibited and may result in immediate account suspension, criminal referral, or civil liability:
TermsOfService.section_07_li1: Unauthorized access to another user's account or data, including through credential sharing, session hijacking, or social engineering.
TermsOfService.section_07_li2: Tampering with or attempting to alter AIS data, vessel declarations, emission estimates, or tax calculation inputs.
TermsOfService.section_07_li3: Submitting false or misleading information in registration, exemption applications, or vessel declarations.
TermsOfService.section_07_li4: Automated scraping, mass downloading, or systematic extraction of Platform data without prior written SMCA authorization.
TermsOfService.section_07_li5: Reverse engineering, decompiling, or attempting to extract source code or proprietary algorithms of the Platform.
TermsOfService.section_07_li6: Using the Platform or data derived from it for commercial intelligence products, third-party maritime tracking services, or competitive analysis without an SMCA data license.
TermsOfService.section_07_li7: Interfering with the availability of the Platform through denial-of-service attacks, excessive automated requests, or abuse of the API.
TermsOfService.section_07_li8: Disclosing confidential Platform data (other than one's own records) to unauthorized parties.
TermsOfService.section_08_p1: The Green Gate platform, including its source code, design, algorithms, maritime carbon calculation models, dashboard layouts, and documentation, is the sovereign intellectual property of the Republic of Somaliland, administered by the Ministry of Finance. All rights reserved.
TermsOfService.section_08_p2: Users are granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to access and use the Platform solely for their authorized purposes as defined in these Terms. No license is granted to reproduce, distribute, sublicense, or create derivative works from Platform content.
TermsOfService.section_08_p3: Data submitted by users (vessel data, company information) remains the property of the submitting party but is licensed to the SMCA for all purposes necessary to fulfil its statutory mandate, including tax enforcement, carbon reporting, and audit record-keeping.
TermsOfService.section_09_highlight: The Republic of Somaliland asserts full sovereign control over all data generated, collected, processed, and stored within the Green Gate platform. Data sovereignty is a non-negotiable principle of this platform and is guaranteed under the Maritime Carbon Act 2024 and applicable Somaliland data protection legislation.
TermsOfService.section_09_p1: The following guarantees apply to all data processed by the Platform:
TermsOfService.section_09_li1: State Ownership: All data generated through the operation of the Platform — including AIS tracking records, tax calculations, emission estimates, audit logs, and carbon credit registries — remains the sovereign property of the Republic of Somaliland, administered by the SMCA on behalf of the Ministry of Finance.
TermsOfService.section_09_li2: Jurisdictional Hosting: All primary data storage infrastructure shall be located within the jurisdiction chosen by the subscribing State or, at minimum, within a jurisdiction offering equivalent data protection standards. The SMCA shall provide written certification of data hosting locations upon request.
TermsOfService.section_09_li3: No Third-Party Transfer: No data shall be transferred to, shared with, or made accessible to any third party — including technology vendors, subcontractors, or foreign governments — without the explicit written consent of the SMCA. This includes anonymized or aggregated data unless specifically authorized.
TermsOfService.section_09_li4: Right to Audit: The subscribing State retains the right to conduct independent audits of data storage infrastructure, access controls, encryption standards, and backup procedures at any time, with 10 business days written notice. The SMCA shall facilitate such audits at no additional cost.
TermsOfService.section_09_li5: Data Residency Guarantee: Upon request, the SMCA shall provide a Data Residency Certificate specifying the physical locations of all servers, backup facilities, and disaster recovery sites where Platform data is stored or replicated.
TermsOfService.section_09_warning: Breach of Data Sovereignty: Any unauthorized transfer, replication, or access to sovereign data constitutes a breach of the Maritime Carbon Act 2024 and may result in criminal prosecution under Somaliland law, contract termination, and claims for damages.
TermsOfService.section_10_highlight: All users of the Green Gate platform have an unconditional right to export their own data at any time, in open and documented formats, without vendor lock-in restrictions. This right is guaranteed regardless of account status, contractual disputes, or payment obligations.
TermsOfService.section_10_p1: The Right to Data Export includes the following guarantees:
TermsOfService.section_10_li1: Full Data Export: Users may request a complete export of all data associated with their account, including vessel records, transaction history, invoices, emission calculations, audit logs, and dispute records. Export is available in CSV, JSON, and PDF formats.
TermsOfService.section_10_li2: Delivery Timeline: The SMCA shall deliver requested data exports within a maximum of 72 hours from the receipt of a valid export request. Automated self-service exports (via the Platform dashboard) shall be available immediately for datasets under 50 MB.
TermsOfService.section_10_li3: Open Formats: All exported data shall be delivered in open, documented, machine-readable formats (CSV with headers, JSON with schema documentation, PDF/A for invoices). No proprietary or encrypted formats that require SMCA-specific software to read.
TermsOfService.section_10_li4: No Vendor Lock-In: The data export format shall be sufficiently documented and standardized to allow migration to any alternative platform or system without loss of data integrity. The SMCA shall provide a Data Dictionary document with each export upon request.
TermsOfService.section_10_li5: Post-Termination Retention: Following contract termination or account deactivation, the SMCA shall retain all user data for a minimum of 90 calendar days, during which the user may request a final data export. TermsOfService.section_11_li1: The SMCA and the Ministry of Finance are not liable for indirect, consequential, special, or punitive damages arising from Platform use, including loss of business, loss of revenue, or commercial losses due to system downtime.

PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPolicy.subtitle: This document explains how the Government of Somaliland, through the Green Gate platform, collects, processes, stores, and protects personal data in connection with maritime carbon tax administration and sovereign environmental monitoring.
PrivacyPolicy.section_01_p1: The Green Gate Maritime Carbon Intelligence Platform is operated by the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development of the Republic of Somaliland (hereinafter "the Ministry") on behalf of the Somaliland Maritime Carbon Authority (SMCA). This platform collects and processes personal and organizational data as part of its statutory mandate to administer maritime carbon taxes, enforce environmental compliance, and generate sovereign revenue from the Gulf of Aden Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
PrivacyPolicy.section_01_highlight: This Privacy Policy is enacted pursuant to the Somaliland Data Protection Act 2023, the principles of the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention, 2014), the IMO Maritime Cyber Risk Management Guidelines (MSC-FAL.1/Circ.3), and the Maritime Carbon Act 2024. Where applicable, we also align our practices with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR 2016/679) for data subjects residing in or connected to European jurisdictions.
PrivacyPolicy.section_01_p2: All processing activities are subject to oversight by the Somaliland Data Protection Commissioner (SDPC) and are recorded in the official national data processing register. This policy applies to all users of Green Gate, including Port Authority officers, Finance Administrators, Shipping Agents, and Armateurs.

PrivacyPolicy.section_02_row3_info: Green Gate — Sovereign Carbon Intelligence Platform

PrivacyPolicy.section_03_cat_c_li2: Vessel technical specifications: gross tonnage, engine power, design speed

PrivacyPolicy.section_05_p1: Processing of personal data on Green Gate is grounded in the following legal bases under the Somaliland Data Protection Act 2023 and aligned international frameworks:
PrivacyPolicy.section_05_li1: Legal Obligation (Art. 6(1)(c) equivalent): Maritime Carbon Act 2024, IMO MARPOL Annex VI, Somaliland Finance Act 2024 — processing is mandatory for tax enforcement and cannot be refused by data subjects operating within the EEZ.
PrivacyPolicy.section_05_li2: Public Task (Art. 6(1)(e) equivalent): Sovereign mandate of the SMCA to monitor, regulate, and report on carbon emissions within Somaliland maritime jurisdiction.
PrivacyPolicy.section_05_li3: Legitimate Interests (Art. 6(1)(f) equivalent): Platform security, fraud prevention, and immutable audit logging — balanced against the rights of data subjects and documented in our Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA/2024-03).
PrivacyPolicy.section_05_li4: Contractual Necessity (Art. 6(1)(b) equivalent): For Shipping Agents and Armateurs who register on the platform, processing is necessary to fulfil the digital services agreement and tax payment obligations.
PrivacyPolicy.section_05_warning: Note on Sensitive Data: Green Gate does not process special categories of personal data (health, biometric, political affiliation) within the meaning of Art. 9 GDPR or equivalent Somaliland law. AIS positional data of vessels is not considered personal data under maritime law but is handled with equivalent security standards.
PrivacyPolicy.section_06_p1: Upon expiry of the applicable retention period, data is securely deleted using cryptographic erasure (overwrite + key destruction) or anonymized for statistical archival. Deletion records are themselves maintained for 2 years.
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_p1: We do not sell, rent, or commercially transfer personal data. Data may be shared only in the following circumstances:
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_li1: International Maritime Organization (IMO): Aggregated, anonymized emission statistics transmitted annually under MARPOL Annex VI reporting obligations.
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_li2: African Union / ITPGRFA: Environmental data shared as part of Somaliland's continental climate commitments — never at individual vessel level without explicit legal basis.
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_li3: Neighboring Coast Guard Authorities (Djibouti, Eritrea): Position data of vessels under investigation for non-compliance, pursuant to bilateral maritime agreements.
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_li4: Ministry of Justice: Audit logs and financial records in the context of criminal investigations, subject to judicial warrant.
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_li5: Technical Subprocessors: Cloud infrastructure and database services operating within Somaliland territory (BER-DC1) or subject to adequate data protection frameworks. All subprocessors are bound by Data Processing Agreements (DPAs).
PrivacyPolicy.section_07_warning: International transfers outside Africa: Any transfer of personal data to countries not recognized as offering adequate protection requires Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and is subject to SDPC approval. No bulk transfer of vessel owner or operator data is made to non-adequate third countries without explicit authorization.
PrivacyPolicy.section_08_p1: Subject to applicable Somaliland law and operational constraints, data subjects have the following rights. Certain rights may be limited where they would interfere with mandatory legal processing obligations (e.g., tax enforcement, audit immutability):

PrivacyPolicy.section_08_row2_limitation: Audit log entries are immutable by design — cannot be altered

PrivacyPolicy.section_08_row4_limitation: Does not apply to active tax enforcement processing

PrivacyPolicy.section_08_row7_limitation: Always available — see contact details below
PrivacyPolicy.section_08_p2: To exercise your rights, submit a written request to dpo@smca.gov.sl with proof of identity. We will respond within 30 calendar days. Complex or multiple requests may be extended by an additional 60 days with notification.
PrivacyPolicy.section_09_highlight: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is a mandatory radio transponder system under IMO SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19. AIS data broadcast by vessels in the Somaliland EEZ is received by sovereign shore-based receivers and is considered publicly accessible technical data under international maritime law. Its collection and use for safety, environmental, and tax enforcement purposes does not require individual vessel owner consent.
PrivacyPolicy.section_09_p1: Within Green Gate, AIS data is used exclusively for: (i) identifying vessels within the EEZ for carbon tax assessment, (ii) calculating estimated CO₂ emissions based on vessel speed, position, and engine specifications, (iii) generating pro-forma invoices and compliance notices, and (iv) populating the Command Center map display for authorized officers.
PrivacyPolicy.section_09_p2: AIS position data is never used for commercial tracking, sold to third parties, or shared beyond the purposes listed above. Raw AIS feeds are retained for 2 years and then purged from primary systems.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_p1: Green Gate implements a multi-layered security architecture in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the IMO Maritime Cyber Risk Management guidelines, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF 2.0):
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li1: Encryption at rest: AES-256 for all stored data, with hardware security modules (HSMs) for key management at BER-DC1.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li2: Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3 for all API and web traffic. Older TLS versions (≤1.2) are rejected at the load balancer.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li3: Access control: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with least-privilege principles. All privileged actions require MFA. Superadmin actions require dual authorization.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li4: Immutable audit logging: All operator actions are SHA-256 hash-chained and stored in a tamper-evident append-only log.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li5: Penetration testing: Annual independent penetration tests by certified third parties. Results disclosed in the Security Audit report.
PrivacyPolicy.section_10_li6: Incident response: Data breach notification to the SDPC within 72 hours, affected data subjects within 5 business days, in accordance with Art. 33–34 GDPR equivalent.
PrivacyPolicy.section_11_p1: Green Gate uses strictly necessary cookies and session tokens only. No advertising, analytics, or tracking cookies are used.
PrivacyPolicy.section_11_p2: Sessions expire automatically after 15 minutes of inactivity as a security measure. This cannot be disabled by users. Session tokens are invalidated server-side on logout and cannot be reused.

PrivacyPolicy.section_12_p1: If you believe your privacy rights have been violated, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Somaliland Data Protection Commissioner (SDPC) at any time, without prejudice to any other administrative or judicial remedy. The SDPC contact is available at sdpc.gov.sl.
PrivacyPolicy.section_12_highlight: This Privacy Policy was last reviewed and approved by the Somaliland Data Protection Officer on March 1, 2025. Changes to this policy will be published at least 30 days before taking effect, with notification to all registered platform users via email.

SecurityAudit.title: Security Audit Report
SecurityAudit.subtitle: This document presents the results of the Green Gate platform security audit, including architecture review, penetration test findings, compliance assessment against ISO 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, and IMO Maritime Cyber Risk Management guidelines, and the SMCA security roadmap.
SecurityAudit.section_01_highlight: Green Gate has been awarded ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for its Information Security Management System (ISMS) covering the Berbera Data Center (BER-DC1) and all platform components. The annual external audit was conducted by Bureau Veritas Certification (accredited by UKAS) in January 2025. No critical or high-severity findings remain open as of the date of this report.
SecurityAudit.section_02_p1: The 2025 annual security audit was conducted between January 6 and January 31, 2025 by an independent team consisting of:
SecurityAudit.section_02_li1: External Auditor: Bureau Veritas Certification — ISO 27001 Lead Auditors (LA-27001 certified)
SecurityAudit.section_02_li2: Penetration Testing Team: CyberNile Security Ltd. (Nairobi / Djibouti) — OSCP, CEH, and CISM certified testers
SecurityAudit.section_02_li3: Internal Audit Oversight: SMCA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and DPO
SecurityAudit.section_02_p2: The audit covered the following components and boundaries:
SecurityAudit.section_02_row2_scope: Authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting
SecurityAudit.section_02_row3_scope: Row-level security, SQL injection, privilege escalation
SecurityAudit.section_02_row4_scope: Data integrity, injection points, unauthorized access
SecurityAudit.section_02_row5_scope: Firewall rules, network segmentation, VLAN isolation
SecurityAudit.section_02_row6_scope: Pod security policies, secrets management, image scanning
SecurityAudit.section_03_p1: Green Gate is deployed on a sovereign, air-gap-capable infrastructure stack at BER-DC1, Berbera, Somaliland. The architecture follows a defense-in-depth model with multiple independent security layers:
SecurityAudit.section_03_li1: Perimeter: DDoS-mitigation appliances (Arbor Networks), ingress filtering, and a Web Application Firewall (WAF) with custom ruleset for maritime API patterns. All external traffic terminates at the WAF before reaching application servers.
SecurityAudit.section_03_li2: Network Segmentation: Production, staging, and management networks are physically separated on dedicated VLANs with inter-VLAN routing restricted by hardware firewall (Fortinet FortiGate 600E). AIS data ingestion network is isolated from the application network.
SecurityAudit.section_03_li3: Application Layer: Next.js frontend served from hardened Node.js instances. Go backend API with request signing, rate limiting (100 req/min per authenticated user), and strict input validation via Zod schemas.
SecurityAudit.section_03_li4: Database Layer: PostgreSQL (Supabase) with Row-Level Security (RLS) policies enforced at the database level for all tables. Column-level encryption for financial data using pgcrypto with HSM-stored keys.
SecurityAudit.section_03_li5: Audit Layer: Dedicated append-only audit database with SHA-256 hash chaining. The audit service runs in an isolated container with no write access to production data — only receives events via an authenticated write-only API.
SecurityAudit.section_03_li6: Secrets Management: HashiCorp Vault (BER-DC1 instance) for all secrets, API keys, and database credentials. No secrets stored in environment variables or container images. Automatic secret rotation every 90 days.
SecurityAudit.section_04_row1_implementation: 4 roles: PORT_OFFICER, FINANCE_ADMIN, COMPLIANCE_AUDITOR, SUPERADMIN — enforced at API and DB levels
SecurityAudit.section_04_row2_implementation: TOTP (RFC 6238) mandatory for SUPERADMIN; available for all users; enforced by policy for all financial operations
SecurityAudit.section_04_row3_implementation: JWT with 15-min expiry, HTTP-only cookies, SameSite=Strict, automatic renewal on activity, server-side invalidation on logout
SecurityAudit.section_04_row4_implementation: SUPERADMIN actions require dual-approval workflow. All privileged sessions recorded and reviewed weekly.
SecurityAudit.section_04_row5_implementation: Min 8 chars, complexity required, bcrypt hashing (cost factor 12), no credential reuse for 12 cycles, HaveIBeenPwned API check on registration
SecurityAudit.section_04_row6_implementation: Account lockout after 5 failed attempts; progressive delay; CAPTCHA after 3 failures; IP-level rate limiting
SecurityAudit.section_04_row7_implementation: Certificate-based SSH only (no password auth). Bastion host required. All sessions logged and recorded.
SecurityAudit.section_04_row8_implementation: Bearer token (JWT) for all API requests; API keys for service-to-service (HMAC-SHA256 signed); no API key in URL
SecurityAudit.section_05_row2_algorithm: AES-256-CBC with unique key per backup set
SecurityAudit.section_05_row5_key_mgmt: Offline root key — air-gapped signing ceremony
SecurityAudit.section_05_p1: All cryptographic modules used in Green Gate are FIPS 140-3 validated (certificates #4765, #4822). Cipher suites below TLS 1.3 are disabled at the load balancer. Export-grade, null, and RC4 cipher suites have never been enabled.
SecurityAudit.section_06_highlight: The Green Gate audit trail is the cornerstone of platform accountability. Every user action, policy change, data access, and system event generates an immutable audit log entry. Entries cannot be deleted, modified, or purged by any user — including SUPERADMIN. The only permitted operation is append.
SecurityAudit.section_06_li1: Hash chaining: Each log entry includes the SHA-256 hash of the previous entry, forming a verifiable chain. Any tampering with a historical entry invalidates all subsequent hashes, making manipulation detectable immediately.
SecurityAudit.section_06_li2: Write-only audit API: The audit service exposes only a POST endpoint. No GET (read), PUT (update), or DELETE endpoint exists at the service level. Read access is via a separate read-only replica.
SecurityAudit.section_06_li3: Daily off-site backup: The full audit log is backed up daily to an air-gapped archive system at the Ministry of Justice. Backup integrity is verified by Ed25519 signatures.
SecurityAudit.section_06_li4: Chain integrity checks: An automated job runs every 6 hours to verify the integrity of the entire hash chain. Alerts are sent to the CISO and SMCA Director if any inconsistency is detected.
SecurityAudit.section_06_li5: Legal standing: The audit log has been accepted as admissible electronic evidence in Somaliland Commercial Court proceedings (Case SCC-2024-117). Its integrity is certified by the National Forensic Institute.
SecurityAudit.section_07_li1: DDoS Protection: Arbor Networks Sightline (hardware) + Cloudflare Magic Transit for volumetric attack mitigation. Tested capacity: up to 40 Gbps. Last DDoS incident: none recorded in 2024.
SecurityAudit.section_07_li2: WAF: ModSecurity with OWASP CRS v3.3.4 + custom rules for maritime API endpoints. Average false positive rate: 0.02%.
SecurityAudit.section_07_li3: Intrusion Detection/Prevention (IDS/IPS): Suricata deployed on all network segments. Signatures updated every 4 hours. Alerts trigger automated response playbooks (Shuffle SOAR).
SecurityAudit.section_07_li4: Zero-Trust Network Access (ZTNA): Administrative access to BER-DC1 infrastructure requires Cloudflare Access (ZTNA) with identity verification, even from internal VPN. Implemented Q4 2024.
SecurityAudit.section_07_li5: AIS Data Isolation: AIS receiver network is physically air-gapped from the internet. Data is transferred to the application network via a one-way data diode (Waterfall Security WF-500). No return path exists.
SecurityAudit.section_07_li6: BGP Security: SMCA AS number protected by RPKI (Route Origin Authorization). All BGP sessions use MD5 authentication and are filtered by prefix lists.
SecurityAudit.section_08_warning: Responsible Disclosure: This public report contains a summary of findings only. Detailed technical findings, proof-of-concept exploits, and remediation code are classified and available only to the SMCA CISO, DPO, and authorized Ministry of Justice representatives under NDA.
SecurityAudit.section_08_row1_remediation: Additional RBAC middleware check — patched Feb 2025
SecurityAudit.section_08_row3_remediation: CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options headers added — patched Jan 2025
SecurityAudit.section_08_row4_remediation: Generic error responses in production — patched Jan 2025
SecurityAudit.section_08_row5_category: Rate limiting bypass via IPv6 rotation (internal)
SecurityAudit.section_08_row5_remediation: IP normalization + rate limit by JWT identity — patched Feb 2025
SecurityAudit.section_08_highlight: No Critical or High-severity findings were identified in the Q1 2025 penetration test. All Medium findings were remediated within 15 days of disclosure. No data breach, unauthorized access, or privilege escalation was achieved during the authorized testing period. The penetration testing team awarded the platform a security maturity score of 8.2/10.
SecurityAudit.section_09_row03_scope: Cyber risk in Safety Management System
SecurityAudit.section_10_p1: Green Gate operates a formal Vulnerability Management Program (VMP) compliant with ISO 27001:2022 Annex A.8.8:
SecurityAudit.section_10_li1: Continuous scanning: Automated vulnerability scanning runs daily on all containers (Trivy), dependencies (Dependabot + Snyk), and infrastructure (Tenable.io). Results are triaged within 24 hours.
SecurityAudit.section_10_li2: Patch SLAs: Critical — 24 hours; High — 7 days; Medium — 30 days; Low — 90 days. Emergency patching process exists for zero-days (target: 4 hours).
SecurityAudit.section_10_li3: Dependency management: Node.js and Go dependencies are pinned with lockfiles. All transitive dependencies are reviewed. npm audit and go mod verify run in CI/CD pipeline.
SecurityAudit.section_10_li4: Zero-day policy: Active threat intelligence feeds (CISA KEV, CERT-EU, AfricaCERT). The SMCA is a member of the AfricaCERT national coordination network.
SecurityAudit.section_11_p1: The SMCA maintains a formal Incident Response Plan (IRP) aligned with NIST SP 800-61r3 and ISO/IEC 27035:2023. The plan is tested quarterly via tabletop exercises and annually via a full red team simulation.
SecurityAudit.section_11_row1_procedure: SIEM alerts (Wazuh), IDS triggers, user reports, automated integrity checks
SecurityAudit.section_11_row2_procedure: CISO + Security team triage, severity classification (P1–P4)
SecurityAudit.section_11_row3_procedure: Automated isolation of affected systems; manual override by CISO
SecurityAudit.section_11_row4_procedure: Root cause analysis, patch deployment, configuration hardening
SecurityAudit.section_11_row5_procedure: Service restoration from clean backups; integrity verification
SecurityAudit.section_11_row6_procedure: PIR report, lessons learned, control improvements, SDPC notification if data breach
SecurityAudit.section_11_highlight: Security Incident History 2024: Zero (0) confirmed data breaches. Three (3) failed unauthorized access attempts detected, blocked, and reported to Somaliland CERT. One (1) phishing attempt targeting a Port Officer — blocked by email security gateway. No successful exploitation of the platform was recorded in 2024.
SecurityAudit.section_12_row01_initiative: SOC 2 Type II certification (Security + Availability + Confidentiality)
SecurityAudit.section_12_row02_initiative: Hardware Security Key (FIDO2/WebAuthn) MFA for all SUPERADMIN users
SecurityAudit.section_12_row03_initiative: Zero-Trust Architecture rollout for all internal services (Istio + SPIFFE)
SecurityAudit.section_12_row04_initiative: Real-time Security Information & Event Management (SIEM) upgrade to Wazuh 4.8
SecurityAudit.section_12_row07_initiative: Supply chain security — SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) publication
SecurityAudit.section_12_row08_initiative: CIS Controls v8 IG2 — achieve full 18/18 implementation
SecurityAudit.section_12_row09_initiative: AfricaCERT formal membership and threat-sharing agreement
SecurityAudit.section_12_p1: Security improvements are tracked in the SMCA Information Security Continuous Improvement Log (ISCIL/2025) and reviewed monthly by the CISO, DPO, and SMCA Director. Progress is reported annually to the Ministry of Finance and included in the next edition of this public Security Audit report.
SecurityAudit.section_12_warning: Responsible Disclosure Program: The SMCA operates a responsible disclosure program for security researchers. If you discover a security vulnerability in Green Gate, please report it to security@smca.gov.sl with PGP encryption (key available at smca.gov.sl/pgp). We commit to acknowledging reports within 48 hours and resolving confirmed vulnerabilities within our standard SLAs. We do not pursue legal action against researchers who follow responsible disclosure principles.
